# Lockfiles

Read these rules when a lockfile check fails or an install is broken. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="nr-64"></a>

## NR-64: One lockfile per installation root `[GAP]`

> One authoritative lockfile per installation root.

Old number: 6.1.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check lockfiles`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The check reads the name package-lock.json only. Add npm-shrinkwrap.json next to hardhat/v3/package-lock.json: npm uses the shrinkwrap file and ignores package-lock.json, so the committed lockfile that every lockfile check reads (6.1.2, 6.1.3, 3.3.4) is no longer the one installed. Nothing fails. Fix: issue I-113.

Issues: I-01, I-113.

Ordinary members have none (their installation root's lock
covers them); a standalone project keeps its own, and so does a non-member consumer registered in `consumerTests`,
because its isolated copy is an independent installation root. A workspace MEMBER registered as a consumer (a Hardhat
template) still has none: its installation root locks it, and `test-consumer` resolves its isolated copy fresh. Consumer
lockfiles are immutable except through `test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock`, which refuses a member.

```text
✅ ordinary workspace member                    <installation root>/package-lock.json only
✅ standalone consumer                         <consumer>/package-lock.json
✅ workspace member registered as a consumer   <installation root>/package-lock.json only (fresh isolated resolve)
❌ ordinary workspace member                    nested package-lock.json
```

`test-consumer` derives each consumer's install mode: it replays a committed lockfile with `npm ci --install-links`,
and runs `npm install --install-links` for a workspace member (none by policy) or for an isolated consumer that lacks
one, which prints a warning. `--ci` turns that warning into an error and changes nothing else.

<a id="nr-65"></a>

## NR-65: No extraneous lockfile nodes `[HOLD]`

> No lockfile carries an extraneous node.

Old number: 6.1.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check extraneous`

npm writes `"extraneous": true` on a package it knows about but
cannot reach from the declared graph — nothing in any `package.json` asks for it. It is what a RETARGETED dependency
leaves behind: the edges move to the new target, the old node is demoted rather than deleted, and the lockfile goes on
naming a package that is no longer in the tree. Retargeting the Hardhat plugins from `<vN-1>`'s payload to `<vN>`'s left
exactly that in three lockfiles at once.

npm will not install it, which is precisely why it survives: nothing breaks, so nobody notices. The cost is that the
lockfile stops being the record of what a clean machine gets, and the stale line reads like a real dependency to the
next person auditing it — a retired generation still apparently in the tree long after the switch. It outlives every
incremental install; only rebuilding the tree drops it.

```text
❌ "../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg": { "extraneous": true }   after the plugin moved to <vN>/pkg
✅ rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install               the node is gone, the edges stay
```

Both lockfile shapes are read — `packages` (lockfileVersion 2 and 3) and the legacy nested `dependencies` (version 1)
— so an older file cannot pass vacuously.

## NR-66: Consumer lockfiles pin the central versions `[GAP]`

> An isolated consumer lockfile pins every published payload at its `versions.json` version, resolved to the payload its depender names.

Old number: 6.1.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check consumer-lockfiles`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Two changes pass. (1) A registry resolution: set the node's "resolved" to the npmjs.com tarball URL of the same name at the versions.json version. payloadFor matches a non-file: node by name (consumer-lockfiles.ts:282-284), so the node counts as the declared payload although its path is not the declared directory. (2) A peer link: filePayloadDependencies reads `dependencies` and `devDependencies` only (:301). If hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg moved its host-contracts file: link to peerDependencies, the rule's own example (the lock still resolving <vN-1>/pkg at its own right version) would pass both assertions. Fix: issue I-114.

Issues: I-114.

The lock is what `npm ci` installs for `test-consumer --ci`, so a stale one tests
yesterday's package while every other check reads today's sources. Two assertions per published node: its `version`
equals `versions.json` for the payload its `resolved` path points at, and that path is the one the depender's
`package.json` declares — the consumer's own, and each payload's the lock reached through it. The second is what the
first cannot see: after the Hardhat v3 plugin moved from `<vN-1>`'s host contracts to `<vN>`'s, its consumer lock still
recorded `@fhevm/hardhat-plugin-v3@<N-1>.0` depending on `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg`; both versions were correct
for the files they named, and both files were the wrong ones. A member consumer has no lock of its own ([NR-64](../entries/NR-64.md)) and is
not graded here.

```text
❌ "node_modules/@fhevm/hardhat-plugin-v3": { "version": "<N-1>.0", "resolved": "file:../../pkg" }
   versions.json: "./hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg": "<N>.0-0"
❌ "node_modules/@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": { "resolved": "file:../../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN-1>/pkg" }
   hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg/package.json: "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg"
✅ fhevm-npm test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock ./hardhat/v3/plugin/test-consumer/esm
```

## NR-67: Member changes invalidate the tree `[HOLD]`

> A member rename or a `workspaces` edit invalidates the tree, not just the lock.

Old number: 6.2.1.

Check: impossible.

npm compares against
`node_modules/.package-lock.json`, so it can report "up to date" while dependencies are missing.

<a id="nr-68"></a>

## NR-68: Delete the tree when packages are missing `[HOLD]`

> When npm says "up to date" and packages are absent, delete the tree.

Old number: 6.2.2.

Check: impossible.

Reinstalling cannot fix it: npm
believes there is nothing to do. Remove `node_modules` (and the lockfile only if placement is stale), then install.

<a id="nr-69"></a>

## NR-69: The local .npmrc applies, not an ancestor `[HOLD]`

> `.npmrc` is read from the local prefix, not from ancestors.

Old number: 6.2.3.

Check: impossible.

Issues: I-01.

A nested workspace root does not inherit the
outer repo's `.npmrc`, so settings like `install-strategy` silently do not apply.

```sh
# ✅ Asked from the nested root, so the answer is the one that governs its installs.
cd hardhat/v2 && npm config get install-strategy

# ❌ Asked from the repo root, reporting the outer .npmrc's value — which hardhat/v2 never reads.
npm config get install-strategy
```
